clips.title: The story
paras: At Camp Taurajo, Tatternack Steelforge investigates reports of sturdy Razormane weapons. He sends travelers past the Field of Giants to recover them, so the Horde can judge the threat.

The Razormane are making unusually durable weapons in the southern Barrens. Most quilboar are dismissed as crude fighters with tools of wood, bone, and stone, so the reports have caught the Horde’s attention. Tatternack Steelforge, an orc smith at Camp Taurajo, is investigating under orders from Warchief Thrall. He doubts the quilboar know proper metalwork and wants proof of whether they have learned new techniques or found better supplies.

Tatternack needs weapons from different parts of the Razormane arsenal to study their craft. South of the Field of Giants, scouts face Razormane war camps and seize weapons from their fighters. Razormane Stalkers carry backstabber daggers, Razormane Seers wield charred wands, and frenzied shock troops bear heavy war shields. Each item offers a glimpse of the martial and mystic arts behind the Razormane push against Horde territory.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: The Razormane quilboars to the south, beyond the Field of Giants, have no skilled blacksmiths from what I am told, but they've apparently started to develop sturdier weapons. I'd like to get my hands on a few different types to learn their techniques if possible.

If you wish to help bring honor to the Horde, then bring me examples of their weapons. Find me a dagger from their stalkers, a wand from their seers, and a shield from their warfrenzy. That should do nicely!

clips.title: Progress
paras: I, too, have doubts that the pathetic quilboars could attain any level of skill in the area of smithing, but I do as the Warchief commands, and I shall learn what I can about the Razormane tribe.
I have had more menial tasks, and I do so willingly if it aids the orc people.

clips.title: Completion
paras: The quilboar are further along than I had expected.
Here, adventurer, take this and get out of my way. I'd better take a closer look at these weapons. We may have underestimated our enemy, and that's the kind of mistake we can't afford to make.
